conventions.componentIdentity: PascalCase shared by Figma master, Astro file and public API
conventions.navigationIcons: Figma-only metadata; never enter Astro folders, registry identities or public APIs
conventions.navigationDividers: one empty Figma-only page named --- between adjacent top-level categories

divergences.reason: Figma stores 45 curated Icon/Material masters while Astro uses one typed inline-SVG renderer.
divergences.instruction: Resolve glyph identities through src/data/design-system/iconLibrary.json; never expose consumer INSTANCE_SWAP or an arbitrary icon prop.

divergences.reason: Figma Style maps to the Astro variant prop, while Figma State variants map to native CSS interaction states.
divergences.instruction: Use variant for primary, secondary, or tertiary. Do not expose a public state prop.

divergences.reason: Figma documents interaction states; Astro renders a native anchor and omits layout-neutral transparent border geometry.
divergences.instruction: Use href for navigation, keep the component free of fixed height and padding, and do not expose a public state prop.

divergences.reason: Figma stores the accessible Label as hidden text; Astro maps the required label prop to aria-label.
divergences.instruction: Always provide label and do not expose arbitrary icon selection.

divergences.reason: Figma uses one unrestricted native Slot; Astro uses the unrestricted default slot with flex wrapping.
divergences.instruction: Do not introduce a Count prop or child-count limit.

divergences.reason: Figma Checked variants map to the initial checked prop, while Figma State variants map to native checkbox interaction states and a private documentation preview hook.
divergences.instruction: Use checked only for the initial value, preserve native checkbox behavior, and do not expose a public state prop.

divergences.reason: The canonical master explicitly uses the Small Component Size mode; Astro fixes data-component-size to small instead of exposing an unsupported size prop.
divergences.instruction: Do not add a public size prop until the canonical Figma master introduces an approved size decision.

divergences.reason: Figma Type maps to the Astro multiline boolean, while Hover and Focus remain native CSS interaction states.
divergences.instruction: Use multiline for textarea semantics and validation for valid or invalid presentation. Do not expose hover or focus as public props.

divergences.reason: Figma uses a fixed 320 px documentation width, while Astro fills the available inline size.
divergences.instruction: Treat the Figma width as a preview fixture. Constrain Input through its composition container in production.

components.name: SearchInput
divergences: Figma Content=Empty|Filled is a presentation axis derived automatically from the native Astro input value; it is not a public prop.
Figma State documents Default, Hover, Focus and Disabled; Astro uses native input pseudo-classes and a private documentation preview hook rather than exposing state.

Figma keeps an optimized standalone field master bound to the canonical Input token and typography contracts because inserting icons into an Input instance would broaden Input's public Figma API; Astro composes the real Input component.
Figma uses _Parts/SearchInput.ClearButton to document the fixed clear action states; Astro renders one native button that clears the value, emits an input event and restores focus.
Figma Component Size modes map to the Astro size prop and data-component-size, with Medium as the shared default.

components.name: Tag
divergences: Figma keeps Tone as a seven-value variant axis; Astro maps it to the tone prop and data-tag-tone.

Figma represents Removable as a Boolean property with _Parts/Tag.RemoveButton documentation states; Astro renders one nested native button and owns hover, focus-visible, pressed and disabled through native interaction states.
Figma uses a TEXT Label property; Astro requires the label prop so the default removeLabel can include the visible value.
Figma Component Size modes map to the Astro size prop and data-component-size, with Small as the shared default.

divergences.reason: Figma MCP cannot reorder pages containing unavailable Graphik Regular or Medium text without changing or cloning preserved nodes.
divergences.instruction: Treat targetOrder as canonical. Reorder the affected pages manually in Figma Desktop after Graphik is available; do not modify visual content.

divergences.reason: The populated legacy Scroll page was renamed Sandbox to preserve six reference frames without reparenting.
divergences.instruction: Move the page to the Workspace group manually after Graphik is available; do not delete the frames.
